newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay vetoes law for steel company sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay vetoes law for steel company sell-off.

text.p: Paraguayan President Juan Carlos Wasmosy on Monday vetoed a law allowing the privatization of state-run steelmaker Aceros Paraguayos, a government official said.
"We have vetoed two articles of the law...one of them in order (to defend) the participation of company workers in the privatization process," Treasury Minister Miguel Maidana told reporters.
"The second article vetoed established that the state would assume all debts which have not been properly calculated, which is inadmissible," Maidana said.
The law, passed March 20, allowed the government to finally sell the state-run company whose privatization, planned since 1994, was suspended by the Supreme Court last October.
The court ruled in favor of a challenge presented by workers, who at the time would not have received any company stock.
Under the new law workers will own 20 percent of company shares, valued at $35 million.
The company was built in the 1970s by the military government of General Alfredo Stroessner at a cost of $105 million.
